sentiment: To hear a bird and answer with a drawing: that is the whole of memory — listen, hold, return it as something softer.

stories.title: Show HN: An e-ink frame that hears birds and draws them as 1800s illustrations
stories.summary: A frame that does nothing but listen. A bird sings, and a moment later the thing on the wall answers in ink — not a photograph, not a recording, but a drawing, the way a person of the 1800s might have answered. The machine hears, holds, and returns the sound as something gentler than sound.

stories.title: An update on Wayback Machine access
stories.summary: An archive is only as real as its reachability. The past is held in the exact tone it was written in, then softened only by whether we can still get to it — a page kept against the day someone wants to remember.

stories.title: Apple Reference Image: A New Approach for Verified Photography
stories.summary: A photograph that can prove it was not altered — the held moment staying honest about itself. To keep a thing true is its own kind of tenderness: the light of one afternoon, held intact.
